_comment: Corrections that MOVE already-attributed dialogue lines from a WRONG character to the right one (distinct from unattributed_hand_attribution.json, which only moves lines OUT of the unattributed bucket). Applied by apply_reattributions.py <game> to app/data/<game>/characters.json, AFTER extraction + apply_unattributed. Idempotent: a line is moved only if it is currently under 'from'; re-running is a no-op. The ROOT CAUSE is fixed in extract_game.py (multi-owner primary-NPC disambiguation, verified fresh-vs-fresh), so a future --force re-extract produces the right attribution directly; this file exists to correct the ALREADY-SHIPPED characters.json, which is never re-extracted (extract refuses to overwrite to protect hand-fixes).

dms.reason: Multi-owner conversation: in scene c08-s2_planeyard BOTH McKlusky (Lonestar_Lv1_Captain) and Shannon Half-Sky (Story_Shaman) bind this convo. Nodes 0-17 have no explicit speaker (protobuf field 12 absent) and are the shaman's dialogue about her brother's trapped spirit, but the extractor's arbitrary first-owner tie-break dumped all 18 onto McKlusky. Confirmed by the GM stage direction 'She looks up, watching you warily' and node 23's explicit Shannon actor ref. McKlusky's own lines (18, 20-22, 24-25, explicit refs) and Officer Aguirre (19) stay put.

PARTY-SLOT PLACEHOLDER. Node 1's speaker ref (field 12) points at scene c10-s1_planeyardreturn's prop 1a44aec9623331d01000164f, a system_spawner_playerSpawner the designer left named 'Player One (Shaman)'. That is a party SLOT, not a character -- at runtime the game fills it and shows the real party member, which for the Planeyard return is Shannon Half-Sky (confirmed in game: her name and portrait on this line). The extractor took the slot label literally and invented a 'Player One (Shaman)' character, which then got voiced with a deep male narrator voice. Root cause fixed in extract_game.py (party-slot placeholders can never be speakers); this rule corrects the shipped file.

PARTY-SLOT PLACEHOLDER, same class as c10-s1 above. Scene c06-s1_aptsfirstfloor has two player spawners: slot 0 ('Player Character 0') is the PC and never speaks -- the PC's words are input nodes (type 7/8), which the extractor files under the narrator bucket. Slot 1 ('Player Character 1', prop 3ded109a306466d82700003c) is the escort, and in this mission that is Paco. The Sad Old Man's node 0 confirms a companion is present ('you two'). Already voiced in Paco's own picked voice, so this is an attribution move only, no recast.

PARTY-SLOT PLACEHOLDER (slot 1 of c06-s1_aptsfirstfloor). The conversation is named after Paco and the line is 'Once we go upstairs, I'm not leaving until I find Coyote or I'm dead.' Already in Paco's voice; attribution move only.

PARTY-SLOT PLACEHOLDER (slot 1 'Player1' of scene c06-s2_aptstopfloor). Paco is named as the speaker by the dialogue itself: Coyote answers node 2 with "'Bout time you got here, Paco", node 4 opens with the stage direction 'Paco glares', and node 7 replies 'Look... Paco...'. Already in Paco's voice; attribution move only.

PARTY-SLOT PLACEHOLDER (slot 1 'Player 1' of scene c21-s0_pikeplaceconcert). Both nodes open with the stage direction 'Coyote whispers in your ear' as the greeter sends the PC in alone. Already voiced in Coyote's picked voice (Gabby); attribution move only.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. The word 'Patient' in the conversation name matched a generic 'Mental Patient' prop on the OTHER floor (scene c12-s2_mercymental) instead of this conversation's own owner, Lorraine, in c12-s1_mercymental. She is a distinct patient from Donny below: node 1 has her asking who she is supposed to play chess with now that Josie is missing, and names Donny in the third person. Recast in her own voice.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH, same cause as Patient2. Confirmed by the dialogue: node 2 is "Name's Donny. That's my name. DONNY. D. O. N. N. Y." and node 4 repeats it. Keeps the voice it already has (Owen Parker) -- 'Mental Patient' empties out entirely once its two patients are split, so there is no longer another character holding that voice.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. 'Father' in the conversation name matched Father Willy Hansen, a Universal Brotherhood priest who appears two chapters later in c21-s1_universalbrotherhood. The speaker is this scene's own owner: prop ci_name 'Symp' (editor label 'Father', portrait Backer_OrkMale_SympathPlan) in c06-s1_aptsfirstfloor -- Zipper's father, raging about Ryker luring his son onto BTL chips. Recast in Symp's voice (Henry Fletcher), which his three existing lines already use.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. 'Delilah' matched 'Delilah Muscle', his bodyguard, over in c17-s2_seamstress. The speaker is Mr. Delilah himself, negotiating runner rates ('for your speed, hired help'll run you about 1,200 a head'). Both already use Alexander Davis, so this is an attribution move only.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. 'Lawyer' matched a 'Lawyer' prop back in c01-s1_3yearsago. These nodes are not the lawyer at all: they are Sam's recorded message, played once the lawyer slots the video ('Hey buddy! Looking good!', 'We're twins... were twins, I guess'). The lawyer's own lines (2, 3, 15, 16, 17) are already under Sam's Lawyer and stay put. Recast in Sam's voice.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. 'Coyote' matched a 'Coyote Ugly' prop in c11-s1_seamstress rather than this scene's own Coyote. It is plainly her: Paco greets her by name and she answers 'Bout time you got here, Paco'. Same voice (Gabby) either way, so attribution move only. Pairs with the party-slot rule above, which moved Paco's half of this same conversation.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. 'Coyote' in the conversation name matched Coyote herself, but she is the SUBJECT here, not the speaker -- she is dead by this point. Every node is Mrs. Kubota: 'Mrs. Kubota's lips are tight', 'Have you seen Coyote, omae?', 'My girl... is not coming back.' Recast in Mrs. Kubota's voice.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH in a two-hander. 'Harlequin' matched his prop in c22-s1_telestrianoffice and swallowed six of Telestrian's lines. They are his by content: 14/15 are the deductions speech ('This is simple accounting... Business'), and 40-43 are him agreeing to call the Zoning Board and sneering 'So your reward for saving the world is to keep your favorite bar open for business?'. The surrounding nodes are already James. Harlequin's own narration (0, 2, 23, 24, 38) stays put. Recast in Telestrian's voice.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. 'Letter' matched a 'Letter' prop in c21-s1_universalbrotherhood; the readable in this scene is the 'Data Pad' prop of c21-s2_brotherhood-s, which is the name the game shows. Same object, right label. Keeps its existing reading voice (Isla Kensington, set as a per-line override).

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. 'Quoth' matched the prop labelled plain 'Quoth' in c26-s0_pikeplacefinale; in his own office scene the prop is 'Mr. Quoth'. Same character, same voice (Adam Lefevre), so attribution move only. The c26 lines keep the label that scene gives him.

CROSS-SCENE NAME MATCH. The node's own stage direction identifies him: 'The man with the cyberdeck calmly speaks with a heavily digitized voice', and the room description in node 0 has 'a chromed out decker argues loudly with an armed thug'. He announces 'This is a Yakuza operation.' Keeps the digitized take already generated for him.
